inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 126.05M basic shares on the FY2026 10-K cover (2026-07-31) plus ~1.85M dilutive awards (FY26 diluted 128.1M vs basic 126.3M weighted). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; no equity was issued for Filtration Group (debt-funded).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement ShareBasedCompensation $179M (SEC XBRL companyfacts). Parker does not tag a separate net-share-settlement withholding line; the amount is immaterial (<$50M) and is not added, so owner FCF is marginally overstated.
inputs.net_debt_basis: PRO FORMA for Filtration Group (closed 2026-08-13, after the balance-sheet date). FY26 10-K debt = non-current 6,766 + current 1,754 (CP ~1,048 + current maturities 706) = 8,520. The Metrics CSV TotalDebt of 9,226 double-counts the 706 current portion (LongTermDebt 7,472 already includes it) -- same XBRL trap as KEYS/NDSN. Plus 9,250 Filtration Group consideration, debt-funded ($7.75B new facilities + CP/notes) = 17,770 gross; less 501 cash = 17,269. Operating lease liabilities (213) excluded: US GAAP operating lease cost is already inside EBITDA (treatment B). Pension liability (224) and NCI (9) immaterial and not bridged.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.15 -> cost of equity ~10.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (4.0% after tax) at ~15% debt weight post-Filtration Group -> WACC ~9.1%, used as 9.0% in all three scenarios. Cyclicality is priced in the bear scenario's flows, not via a premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): US GAAP operating-lease cost sits inside operating income/EBITDA; lease liabilities excluded from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI of $9M is immaterial; flows not adjusted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, cyclical US industrial) per dcf-methods routing; first valuation of PH, no prior DCF. FY0 build: GAAP operating income 5,068 + D&A 937 (depreciation 353 + intangible amortization 584) + SBC 179 = 6,184 pre-SBC EBITDA (28.8%); the margin path starts ~50bp lower (28.3% standalone FY0-equivalent) to absorb non-service pension/other expense (~104) and restructuring cash that sit between operating income and pretax income. Unlevered cash tax: 1,064 paid + 401 interest x 21% shield = ~1,148 on EBIT 5,068 = 22.6%, used as 22.5%. FILTRATION GROUP ($9.25B, closed 2026-08-13) is consolidated in BOTH flows and debt: assumed ~$1.9B annual revenue at ~24% EBITDA pre-synergy (~20x EBITDA paid), ~10.5 months in FY27 (+~8pp of FY27 growth) and the 1.5-month stub in FY28 (+~1pp). FY27 guidance of 5.5-8.5% reported/organic growth was issued 2026-08-06, before the close, and is read as excluding Filtration Group (reported and organic ranges are identical, which is impossible if a ~$1.9B acquisition were inside). The ~$220M year-3 synergy target is in the EBITDA ramp. CIRCOR Aerospace ($2.55B, ~$270M sales at >40% EBITDA, ~23x) is still pending regulatory approval and is EXCLUDED from both flows and debt -- treated as roughly value-neutral at the price paid; closing it would add ~$2.55B debt and ~$110M EBITDA. The working-capital charge (-12% of revenue change) also hits the acquired FY27/FY28 revenue step, which arrives with its own working capital: a conservative ~$200M (~$1.6/share) overcharge left in rather than special-cased. D&A path steps up for Filtration Group amortization then glides to 2.6% of revenue by Y10 so terminal D&A sits only modestly above capex (no perpetual amortization tax shield). Buybacks ($1,262M FY26, $1,766M FY25) fund the flat share count; Parker is a genuine repurchaser.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management FY2031 framework (4-6% organic) cross-checked to revenue 3yr CAGR 4.1%; equity CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 12.9% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 8.4%, and EPS CAGRs (16-21%) are inflated by the Meggitt (FY23) acquisition, margin expansion and buybacks. Neither equity nor EPS growth is a sustainable revenue growth rate; the 5-yr revenue CAGR itself includes Meggitt. Organic growth through the cycle has been ~3-5%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (SBC deducted) run slightly ABOVE reported FCF CAGRs: SBC (~0.8% of revenue) is growing slower than cash flow, so no stock-paid-growth flag. FY21-26 FCF growth includes Meggitt and the post-FY23 margin step-up; FY23 is depressed by Meggitt deal costs.

base.narrative: FY27 organic growth at the 7% guidance midpoint plus ~10.5 months of Filtration Group; then 4.5-5% (mid of the 4-6% organic framework) fading to 3%. EBITDA margin climbs ~200bp to 30.5% by FY32 -- most, not all, of the 30% adjusted-segment-margin target plus Filtration Group synergies.

bull.narrative: Synchronised industrial recovery plus an aerospace upcycle: FY27 lands at the top of guidance, the $12.8B backlog converts, data-centre liquid cooling and electrification add a point of growth, and the 30% FY31 margin target is beaten with full Filtration Group synergies.

bear.narrative: FY27 at the bottom of guidance, then an industrial/off-highway downturn in FY29 (-6% revenue, ~350bp decremental margin) coinciding with a Boeing/Airbus build-rate wobble, while Filtration Group integration slips and synergies arrive late. Margins recover only to ~28% -- the FY26 level -- and the 30% target is never reached.

scenario_narratives.base: Parker executes the FY27 guide (7% organic midpoint) and consolidates Filtration Group, then grows mid-single-digit organically through the industrial and aerospace cycles. The Win Strategy and ~$220M of Filtration Group synergies lift EBITDA margin ~200bp to 30.5%, short of a full hit on the 30% adjusted-segment-margin target. Leverage from the $9.25B deal is serviced from ~$4.5-5B of annual owner FCF; CIRCOR Aerospace is treated as value-neutral.
scenario_narratives.bull: The broad-based recovery management guided to (every vertical positive in FY27 for the first time in years) runs for several years while commercial aerospace OEM rates and defense budgets lift the record $8.5B aerospace backlog into aftermarket annuity revenue. Data-centre liquid cooling and electromechanical actuation become real growth vectors, organic growth runs above the 4-6% framework, and margins beat the 30% target to ~32% EBITDA.
scenario_narratives.bear: Diversified Industrial (67% of sales) rolls over: agriculture/off-highway weakness spreads to construction and general industrial capex, tariffs and input inflation squeeze price-cost, and a commercial aerospace build-rate setback hits just as two large debt-funded integrations stretch management. Revenue falls ~6% in FY29, margins drop to ~26% before recovering to the FY26 level, synergies slip, and the exit multiple compresses to a cyclical 14x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 20% from the 15% default because the company enters an industrial cycle with leverage up ~2x after Filtration Group and a second deal pending, and the industrial cycle has not been repealed. Base 50%: guidance, backlog and the margin framework are well-anchored and Parker has a long record of hitting margin targets. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs a multi-year synchronised industrial + aerospace upcycle AND clean execution on two integrations.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Parker is valued as a high-quality cyclical industrial on a strict owner-FCF basis: SBC expensed, share count flat, Filtration Group consolidated pro forma in both flows and net debt, and cyclicality carried in the bear scenario's flows rather than a discount-rate premium. The market price capitalises a premium industrial multiple that the 9% WACC owner-FCF build does not reach without bull-case margins.
key_risks_to_valuation: Filtration Group revenue/EBITDA (~$1.9B / ~24%) are assumptions, not filed figures; the Q1 FY27 10-Q (Nov 2026) will give the first consolidated read
Pro-forma net debt assumes the full $9.25B was debt-funded; any cash or CP mix changes the bridge dollar-for-dollar ($1B = ~$7.8/share)
Industrial cycle timing: the bear case's FY29 downturn is a timing judgment
CIRCOR Aerospace excluded; at ~23x EBITDA it is mildly value-dilutive to this model if it closes
Terminal value is the majority of EV; WACC +/-1pp moves value ~15-20%
